messages:
lina: FYI — customer says their promo is valid in the dashboard but the API returns 400 / invalid_code when they paste it into checkout. They sent the raw string and a screenshot.
lina: USER QUOTE (pasted): `X0LO-9O1L`  \n(screenshot: https://redwood.screenshots/test/IMG_1234.png)
sam: Can you share the account email and the exact curl they used? Also whether they typed it or pasted from somewhere.
lina: Account: jordan@example.com. Customer says they pasted from a PDF partner email. I reproduced quickly by copy/pasting the code from the screenshot into our web checkout and got the same 400 from the promo API.
ray: paste the curl you used, lina?
lina: I used the storefront API curl they provided:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/promos/redeem" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -d '{"code":"X0LO-9O1L","account_email":"jordan@example.com"}'
```

response: `{"error":"invalid_code","message":"Promo code not found or expired"}`

sam: interesting. I grabbed the bytes of the string from the screenshot vs the customer's copy. Can you try a manual normalization check, ray?
ray: I ran a quick python snippet to inspect codepoints for both strings. From the screenshot copy: `['X', '0', 'L', 'O', '-', '9', 'O', '1', 'L']` (ord -> [88,48,76,79,45,57,79,49,76])\nFrom the customer's pasted string: `['X', 'O', 'L', 'O', '-', '9', 'O', '1', 'L']` (ord -> [88,79,76,79,45,57,79,49,76])
ray: So the second character is capital letter O (U+004F) vs digit zero (U+0030) in the screenshot vs paste. Dashboard copy button had the zero but partner's PDF used a font where O and 0 look identical and their copy pipeline converted it to O.
sam: Ah — homoglyph issue then. Our promo matching is strict: we expect digits/letters as-is and we don't currently try to normalize common confusables.
lina: Customer insists they copied exactly and the partner email is what's confusing. They asked if we can manually apply the credit because they need it today.
amelia: I can grant the credit manually. Lina, please confirm the account email and the code they pasted and I'll create a one-off credit of the same promo value and mark the partner ticket.
lina: Confirmed: jordan@example.com; pasted code: `X O L O - 9 O 1 L` (they reported spaces only for clarity). Please grant same amount, status: pending.
amelia: Done — manual credit applied and a support note added: "Manual grant due to homoglyph mismatch in partner email copy." Transaction id: txn_3hG7. I also attached steps for product to consider user-facing help.
ray: For engineering follow-up: propose we add a UX hint on the dashboard/copy button and add a lightweight normalization check server-side that warns users when submitted code contains likely-confusable pairs (0/O, 1/l/I, S/5, B/8). Not auto-fixing — just suggest "Did you mean X0LO-9O1L?" and show the normalized candidate.
sam: Agree. Could add a small validation step pre-submit. Low-risk, high UX win.
lina: I'll message partner and customer with the manual grant details and explain the cause. Customer is happy for the workaround.
ray: Filing a follow-up ticket for the promo service: PROMO-1352 — "Add homoglyph detection + user hint for promo codes". Assigning to eng-infra triage.
lina: Closing the support thread with the customer. Thanks all :thumbsup:
